summary_hint: Borrower(s), lender, property, note date, and the loan terms — original principal, rate and rate type, monthly P&I, first-payment and maturity dates — the authoritative source of the mortgage's contractual terms.

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity — the property the note is secured by; match to the loan file

typed_core.name: borrower_names_raw
typed_core.why: identity/disambiguator — signers verbatim (flattened from person[]); a bad name split stays visible

typed_core.name: borrower_name
typed_core.why: identity — first borrower obligated on the note

typed_core.name: borrower_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — co-borrower

typed_core.name: lender_name
typed_core.why: identity — the payee/lender named on the note
typed_core.prompt_hint: The lender name may be the originator, differing from the eventual investor named in an endorsement; distinguish the originating lender from any endorsee

typed_core.name: note_date
typed_core.why: identity/attribution — the note's execution date; CL-6 execution timing; distinguishes an amended/re-executed note
typed_core.prompt_hint: Note date vs first-payment date vs maturity date — three dates that are easily confused; keep all three distinct

typed_core.name: note_city_and_state
typed_core.why: identity — jurisdiction the note recites

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity — links the note to the loan file (confidential)

typed_core.name: original_principal_amount
typed_core.why: processor / CR-8 corroboration — the mortgage principal the payment history tracks
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the principal as figures; principal is written both in words and figures ('$350,000.00 ... three hundred fifty thousand') — use the figure

typed_core.name: interest_rate
typed_core.why: processor — note rate

typed_core.name: rate_type
typed_core.why: processor / disambiguator — fixed vs adjustable determines which special-terms fields apply
typed_core.prompt_hint: Read rate_type first; only populate ARM fields when the note is adjustable, and balloon_* / interest_only_* only when the product recites them

typed_core.name: payment_due_day
typed_core.why: processor — day of month payments are due; anchors lateness

typed_core.name: first_payment_date
typed_core.why: processor / CR-8 corroboration — start of the payment-history window

typed_core.name: maturity_date
typed_core.why: processor — loan term end

typed_core.name: monthly_principal_and_interest
typed_core.why: processor / CR-8 corroboration — the contractual P&I amount

typed_core.name: late_charge_terms
typed_core.why: processor — grace-period days and late-charge %; the tolerance boundary CR-8's lateness check is defined against
typed_core.prompt_hint: Late charge stated as a percentage of overdue P&I plus a grace-period in days ('15 days'); both belong in late_charge_terms

typed_core.name: prepayment_terms
typed_core.why: processor — prepayment penalty presence materially affects program eligibility

typed_core.name: balloon_payment_terms
typed_core.why: processor — a balloon changes the qualifying/fully-amortizing picture (populated only for balloon notes)

typed_core.name: interest_only_or_negative_amortization_terms
typed_core.why: processor — IO / neg-am bears directly on ATR/eligibility (populated only for such products)

typed_core.name: borrower_signature_present
typed_core.why: CL-6 — whether the note is signed (flattened from signature[])
typed_core.prompt_hint: The note is signed but generally not notarized — notarization lives on the deed of trust; do not expect a notary block here

typed_core.name: borrower_signature_date
typed_core.why: CL-6 — execution date of the borrower signature(s)

rejected.name: subject_property_indicator
rejected.reason: a judgment the extractor cannot read faithfully — a note never declares itself the 'subject'; classification/matching decides it (same call as doc 027)

rejected.name: issuer_name
rejected.reason: a note has no issuing organization; the relevant party is the lender/payee -> lender_name

rejected.name: default_and_notice_terms, acceleration_terms
rejected.reason: uniform-instrument boilerplate identical across all standard notes -> no per-loan discriminator; catch-all suffices (flagged)

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: the note's form number (e.g. Form 3200-series) has no consumer rule today; catch-all

rejected.name: statement_period_start / _end, document_issue_date
rejected.reason: a note is not a periodic statement

rejected.name: notary_block
rejected.reason: a note is signed, not notarized (the deed of trust carries the notary)

rejected.name: document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: no discriminating value on a signed note

rejected.name: change_dates_and_index, margin_and_caps, payment_change_terms
rejected.reason: ARM-only object/text; catch-all unless a rate rule is built (no consumer today)

rejected.name: allonge_or_endorsement
rejected.reason: object[] endorsement chain; no in-scope consumer (CR-8 reads the credit report) -> catch-all

rejected.name: borrower_signatures (as a nested list)
rejected.reason: flattened to borrower_signature_present + borrower_signature_date; 1-2 signers do not justify a bespoke list for an out-of-scope rule

encoding_variations: Rate type stated as 'Fixed Rate Note' title vs an ARM note's index/margin recital — rate_type must be read from the instrument type, and it disambiguates which special-terms fields are non-null.
Note date vs first-payment date vs maturity date — three dates that are easily confused; keep all three distinct.
Late charge stated as a percentage of overdue P&I plus a grace-period in days ('15 days'); both belong in late_charge_terms.
Principal written both in words and figures ('$350,000.00 ... three hundred fifty thousand') — use the figure.
Lender name may be the originator, differing from the eventual investor named in an endorsement.

open_questions.q: Both rules are BLOCKED — build now or defer? Per the standard's Tier-3 guidance, a thin doc is 'written when the rule is built.' This doc is Tier-2 (2 rules) but both are blocked.
options: ship the loan-terms typed core now
open_questions.recommendation: ship the loan-terms typed core anyway (it is the authoritative source many future rules will read), but treat the field list as provisional until CL-6/CR-8 unblock

open_questions.q: CR-8's field is on another document. how_engine_checks says it extracts the credit report's mortgage tradeline payment history — nothing on the Note. The direct payment-history field is underivable on this document.
options: record CR-8 as served by the credit-report schema, not this one
open_questions.recommendation: record CR-8 as served by the credit-report schema, not this one; keep the note's terms as corroboration only

open_questions.q: subject_property_indicator (CORE) — fact or judgment? Same as doc 027: a note does not declare itself the subject.
open_questions.recommendation: reject as a conclusion; classification owns it

open_questions.q: Signature handling — flatten vs nest. With 1-2 borrowers and CL-6 out of scope.
open_questions.recommendation: flatten (adopted). Revisit as a nested list only if CL-6 comes in scope and per-signer signed/date is required

open_questions.q: Uniform-instrument boilerplate. default_and_notice_terms / acceleration_terms are CORE but identical on every standard note. Rejected here as no-signal.
open_questions.recommendation: confirm the domain expert agrees they add nothing per-loan before dropping

notes: 21 typed-core fields. Both rules are BLOCKED, so the floor contributes little directly; the count is carried by the catalog CORE loan-terms set, which is the reason this document exists and the corpus of future cheap rules (rate, term, P&I, prepay).

Rule-status caveat: both rules are BLOCKED. CL-6 is post-close / out of scope (execution & notarization). CR-8's how_engine_checks reads the credit report's mortgage tradeline, not the Note — the note's terms (original_principal_amount, monthly_principal_and_interest, first_payment_date) corroborate only.

This is a Fannie/Freddie uniform instrument: default_and_notice_terms and acceleration_terms are boilerplate paragraphs identical across notes — rejected as no per-loan signal (pending domain-expert confirmation).

borrower_name(s), property_address, and loan_number (catalog sensitivity confidential) are typed so they are protected from the raw catch-all; no SSN/DOB appears on a note. Recommend registering none for masking (a recorded note is a public instrument, and the loan number is the link key) — pre_masked=false if registered.

Ambiguity: rate_type classed disambiguator ('processor / disambiguator' — it determines which special-terms fields apply); note_date classed identity with CL-6 in rules ('identity/attribution ... CL-6 execution timing').
